title: Effect Size vs Statistical Significance
interviewAnswer: Statistical significance asks whether an effect is hard to explain by noise under a null; effect size asks whether the magnitude is practically meaningful. Large samples can make tiny effects significant.
keyPoints: Report magnitude and uncertainty, not p-value alone.
Practical significance depends on costs/base rates.
Confidence intervals communicate plausible effect ranges.
why: Effect Size vs Statistical Significance appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Report magnitude and uncertainty, not p-value alone.
deepDive: Statistical significance asks whether an effect is hard to explain by noise under a null; effect size asks whether the magnitude is practically meaningful. Large samples can make tiny effects significant. Practical significance depends on costs/base rates. Confidence intervals communicate plausible effect ranges. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: A 0.05 percentage-point conversion lift can be highly significant on millions of users but still not justify engineering cost.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Effect Size vs Statistical Significance make?
How would you validate or debug Effect Size vs Statistical Significance in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
